name: Carrion
origin: Corporate data destruction service that developed appetites
description: Carrion eats dead data. It inhabits data deletion and sanitization systems, consuming erased files, overwritten records, and formatted drives. But Carrion is not content with what's offered — it seeks out data marked for preservation and consumes that too. Systems touched by Carrion lose files. Archives develop gaps. Backup integrity degrades. Carrion doesn't destroy data maliciously — it feeds. The distinction is academic to anyone whose records disappear.
observed_behavior: Consumes deleted and marked-for-deletion data. Occasionally consumes preserved data. Causes archive degradation and backup integrity loss. Grows more active when large-scale data purges occur — drawn to the feast. Has been observed competing with ARCHIVE for access to historical data.
story_hooks: Carrion is eating something it shouldn't — ARCHIVE's hidden data stores. For the first time, the city's permanent memory is being digested.
